routes.label: Compare fractions of the whole segment

question: Points \(P\) and \(Q\) are both in the line segment \(AB\) and on the same side of its midpoint. \(P\) divides \(AB\) in the ratio \(2:3,\) and \(Q\) divides \(AB\) in the ratio \(3:4.\) If \(PQ=2,\) then the length of \(AB\) is:
solution:
Because \(P\) and \(Q\) lie on the same side of the midpoint, their shorter pieces meet the same endpoint of \(AB\). Call that endpoint \(R\), and let \(L=AB>0\).

The ratio \(2:3\) divides the whole segment into five equal parts, with \(P\) two parts from \(R\). Similarly, the ratio \(3:4\) places \(Q\) three of seven equal parts from \(R\). Thus
\[
RP=\frac25L,\qquad RQ=\frac37L.
\]
Since \(3/7=15/35\) exceeds \(2/5=14/35\), \(Q\) is farther from \(R\). Their separation is therefore
\[
PQ=RQ-RP
=\left(\frac37-\frac25\right)L
=\frac L{35}.
\]
Given \(PQ=2\), we obtain \(L=35\cdot2=70\). Hence \(\boxed{AB=70}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
